heading: Rust crates and helper executables
body:
A desktop, iOS or Android app can declare the crates its native Rust companion needs in `tac.application.rust` in `client/manifest.json` (ADR 0019). `dependencies` applies to every target that links Rust, and `platformDependencies` has `android`, `ios`, `macos`, `linux` and `windows` tables. The iOS app builds them for `aarch64-apple-ios`, or for `aarch64-apple-ios-sim` (`x86_64-apple-ios` on an Intel Mac) in a simulator build; install that target with `rustup target add` first, or the build stops (`TY1605`). The Android app builds them for `arm64-v8a` and `x86_64` with the Android NDK; it needs `rustup target add aarch64-linux-android x86_64-linux-android` and the NDK, or the build stops (`TY1605`). Each version is exact, written `=MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`. A dependency can also set `features` and `defaultFeatures` (true unless set to false). Git, path and registry dependencies and unknown declaration fields are refused at build time (`TY1601`). The app needs at least one native Rust service. These declarations do not supply crates for a service compiled as WebAssembly.

Tachyon builds declared crates offline from `vendor/rust/` at the project root, beside `client/`. Stage the selected host first, for example `ty bundle --target windows --arch arm64 --native`. This writes `dist/windows/project/rust-companion/Cargo.toml` without invoking the platform packager. To prepare the vendored folder, run `cargo vendor --manifest-path dist/windows/project/rust-companion/Cargo.toml vendor/rust` yourself with the sources you intend to use. That preparation step may download crates; a Tachyon bundle never does. Then run the same bundle command without `--native` to package it. Change the staged path when you choose another target or `--out-dir`. Cargo runs with `--offline`, `net.offline=true` and registry source replacement. A missing folder stops the build before Cargo (`TY1605`), and a missing crate fails offline resolution.

`executables` maps a program name to a Rust class file under `client/`. Only desktop apps take them: iOS and Android builds refuse `executables` (`TY1601`), because a mobile app may not start other programs. Names use lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, and there may be at most eight. The name must not match the app executable. The entry class is named after its file and has `pub fn run() -> i32`; Tachyon generates a main function that calls it and uses its result as the exit code. A helper can reach exported companion items through `crate::models` and `crate::<Type>`.

Delegates have stable paths beside the main executable: `<App>/bin/<name>` on Linux, `<App>\bin\<name>.exe` on Windows, and `<App>.app/Contents/MacOS/<name>` on macOS. A helper can resolve that folder from `std::env::current_exe()?.parent()`. macOS helpers are signed ad hoc before the app bundle is signed. Tachyon packages these programs; the app chooses when to start them. No service, login item, autostart entry or elevated helper is registered.
